articles.title: US fashion CEO resigns after physically restraining animal rights activists
articles.summary: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week. The chief executive of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, Steven Kolb, has resigned after he was filmed physically restraining two animal rights activists during an…
body: “After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organisation to begin a new chapter.”
Kolb had been placed on leave on Tuesday pending a review of an incident during a COS show at New York fashion week on Sunday.

In a video, Kolb could be seen trying to restrain two People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) protesters who attempted to disrupt the show in a demonstration against the use of wool by the H&M group, which owns COS.

Kolb pushed a protester, identified as Mason Melito, and covered his mouth. Kolb also wrestled a second protester to the ground, using his arms and a leg to restrain her and putting his hand over her mouth.
points: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week.

articles.title: The Black women who choose to have children on their own: ‘We’re going in eyes open’
articles.summary: With growing support networks online and in person, these moms say they’re changing the narrative around Black single motherhood. When Chamise Alston was ready to have a child, she connected her computer to her TV and scrolled through profiles with her best friend, dismissing people who seemed like…
body: That winter day in 2023, Alston and her friend chose a donor who would help her become pregnant with her now 16-month-old daughter. As a Black woman, she felt empowered taking control of her reproductive destiny.
“I always wanted to be a mom,” said 40-year-old Alston. “Once I realized that there was a route for me to be a mom, sans a relationship, that’s always been my mission.”

Alston is part of a growing number of Black women opting to be single moms by choice (SMBC) through IVF, intrauterine insemination and adoption. Studies show that SMBCs are most likely to be financially stable, educated women in their late 30s. While Black women who choose solo parenting fit a similar profile as their white peers, they face unique challenges. Along with navigating stigmas around Black single motherhood, they also contend with a limited number of Black and brown sperm donors, and sometimes face discriminatory experiences from hospital staff during labor and delivery.

articles.title: Don’t be afraid to be masculine, laugh more, and phone your mum: letters to our sons, by Stephen Graham, Riz Ahmed, Danny Dyer and other wise men
articles.summary: The Adolescence actor and the psychologist Orly Klein asked fathers to write to their sons. The results – from famous dads to the wisdom of strangers – were moving and motivating. Here’s a selection. What can I say?
body: What can I say? From the moment you and your sister were born my heart has been full of a love I never thought was humanly possible. As a baby you were filled with wonder and so much energy. You had a beautiful, mischievous and inquisitive nature, which has always made me smile. You were climbing, running and jumping everywhere. You’d walk into a room wearing shoes that were four times, five times, 10 times too big for you … Sometimes they were ye mother’s.

The sound of your laughter is one of the most beautiful compositions made by nature. I am so blessed to be a part of your life, and our friendship is something I hold dear to my heart. That beautiful bouncing boy has grown into a man who brightens up a room whenever he walks into it.

I have had the pleasure of watching you grow, of watching you learn the lessons of life, like how you conducted yourself when your heart was broken for the first time. To watch you navigate that pain with compassion and come out the other side appreciating your worth without holding on to any resentments, showing your vulnerability to me and your mother and allowing us to guide you through – that was truly admirable.

The results – from famous dads to the wisdom of strangers – were moving and motivating.

articles.title: China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario
articles.summary: Silicon Valley China hawks, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei among them, fear the country surpassing US’s AI lead as much as superintelligence destroying humanity. When reporters asked Donald Trump this week if he supported calls to slow down the development of artificial intelligence out of growing…
body: “We’re leading China in AI,” Trump said. “We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to ⁠keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins.”

Trump was echoing a message the AI industry has put out for years. The US is in a heated technological race with China, companies including Anthropic and OpenAI have argued, and any regulation that would cede the contest risks incalculable economic and political harm.
Even as Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s CEO, led an industry-wide call this week to “pace the frontier”, he declared that the US could only slow down to the point where China could not catch up.

“If we greatly restrain our AI capabilities in the belief that China will do the same, and then China defects, AI could be so powerful that such a defection could lead to their geopolitical dominance,” Amodei warned.

articles.title: “Immerse yourself in the Skims world”: Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede Talk Global Expansion
articles.summary: After a fresh investment round and a $5 billion valuation, Skims has opened its first European flagship in London. Its founders break down the expansion plan.
body: On the Friday night of London Fashion Week, fans congregated outside the new Skims store on Regent Street, as co-founders Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede celebrated the opening of the London flagship with a star-studded party, attended by Troye Sivan, Kim Petras, Tems, and Central Cee. It’s Skims’s first European flagship, and marks a significant milestone as the label continues to invest in major retail expansion beyond the US.

“You can only describe texture and fabrics in so many ways through what you post on socials, and I can do so many educational tutorials explaining all of that. But it’s a really different feeling for people to be able to come here, try on the product, stretch it, feel it, see what fits for [them],” says Kardashian, speaking to Vogue Business at the store. “Even [down to] design of our store and how we merchandise everything, it’s really important to be able to immerse yourself in our Skims world.”

articles.title: Kim Kardashian’s Take on Neutrals Is as Kim Kardashian as You Would Expect
articles.summary: Out and about in London, hanging with boyfriend Lewis Hamilton and attending her Skims store party, Kim Kardashian opted for shimmering, skin-tight nudes.
body: London Fashion Week isn’t usually on the calendar for one Kim Kardashian, but this week brought a special occasion: the launch of her Skims London flagship. Naturally, the night called for not one, not two, but three major looks, all orbiting a palette of fall neutrals. And, of course, it was all very Kim K: body-conscious, glossy, and dialled all the way up.

Kardashian began the evening at the store launch in Ludovic de Saint Sernin, wearing the label’s Mermaid Bi Dress in flesh-toned leather. The gown closely contoured her curves, with a grommet-studded bodice and lace-up slit revealing a sheer underlay beneath. It was a fitting choice given Kardashian’s forthcoming collaboration with the designer, due to launch October 1: a capsule marrying Skims’s shapewear foundations with Saint Sernin’s unapologetically sexy, party-ready signatures.
points: Out and about in London, hanging with boyfriend Lewis Hamilton and attending her Skims store party, Kim Kardashian opted for shimmering, skin-tight nudes.

articles.title: Turmeric’s Unexpected Benefits
articles.summary: Turmeric is proving to be more than a kitchen staple, with growing evidence highlighting its remarkable health benefits
body: Turmeric, the golden flower and root, has been used for a long time across cultures, including my own Indian culture. My parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents have all incorporated turmeric into both their diet, health, and beauty rituals because of its nutrient-rich profile.

Ruhil Badiani, general practitioner at Cornerstone Clinic, agrees. There are a handful of studies that address the ability of curcumin (the active ingredient in turmeric) to manage and reduce inflammation; it can also help with digestion, as well as help neutralize free radicals. Beyond internal use, turmeric is also a popular ingredient in skin care. Turmeric can brighten skin—it works similarly to vitamin C—and I like to add a tiny bit to my homemade face masks (be careful, it stains!).

But if you’re looking for ways to incorporate turmeric into food or curious about taking supplements, this is the guide for you. Read on below to find everything you need to know about the nutritious spice.

articles.title: Suki Waterhouse Gives Her Hair a Disco Update
articles.summary: Performing her track “Weirdo,” Suki Waterhouse tested out the hair tinsel trend from decades gone by.
body: Suki Waterhouse’s aesthetic is built on retro romance: it’s been a subtle transition from Brit it-girl bedheads to boho glam, Birkin-esque hair, and groovy makeup details, leaning more into the ’70s rock star vibes. For her latest performance, the singer—whose 2024 album was called Memoir of a Sparklemuffin —added another vintage element to her signature shaggy blonde hair.

Performing the dreamy “Weirdo” on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Waterhouse threaded fine strands of silver tinsel through her hair, worn straight and just a little longer than the clavi-cut of the moment, with her choppy bangs skimming her brows. The metallic strands were dispersed delicately through her longer layers and concentrated towards the back of the crown, creating something of a reverse halo effect. The finishing touch was a sparkling tiara nestled on top.

The rest of the look stayed within the same whimsical, slightly off-kilter register. Waterhouse performed in a cropped baby-blue Nude Project cardigan and creamy high-waisted knickers, with Tiffany & Co. jewels adding yet more sparkle. Disco dolly.
